sentences.text: Exploring a research collaboration on Baker-Gordon syndrome
We are writing to the Baker-Gordon Syndrome Foundation, which supports families affected by SYT1 changes.
The best-supported mechanism is a dominant-negative effect, where the altered protein blocks the working one.
Gain of function and haploinsufficiency have been suggested but are contested, and a link to calcium-triggered release is unverified.
Your registry, the University of Missouri natural history study and a Cambridge and Melbourne collaboration involve people with this condition.
The natural history study and Project PENGUIN are recruiting.
Aminopyridines are contested, with laboratory evidence only and no patient treatment cited.
We would like to explore a jointly designed study on Baker-Gordon syndrome, shaped with your community from the start: [study question], [design], [sites].
Any participation would follow informed consent and ethics approval, and we would share what we learn with your community.

sections.heading: What we would ask of you

sentences.text: Would you be open to a conversation about whether this idea is useful to the families you serve?
If so, we would value your view on how your community, registry or natural history work could take part, with proper consent and ethics approval.
We are not asking for any personal information about patients or families.
Could we arrange a short call at a time that suits you, perhaps [proposed dates]?
With thanks and warm regards, [researcher name], [institution].
